reason: council-remediation-2026-07-20/agent-P override of prior batch-071 edit. The original linked question text contains literal placeholder '[Not found in provided search results. Requires independent verification of post-Yolanda coastal zoning standards.]' instead of the law name, and the '40-meter no-build zone' premise was a post-Yolanda administrative policy (DENR, 2013) that was later revised to a 'no-dwelling zone' approach based on scientific risk assessment (OPARR). The original rationale 'Post-Yolanda no-build zone: 40 meters from mean high tide... now mandatory in coastal CLUPs post-2014' is not source-supported. The article body of lea-plan-003-06 does NOT cover post-Yolanda no-build zones; it covers PD 1067 easements (3m urban / 20m agricultural / 40m forest) by land classification. This council pass preserves the PD 1067 framing and clarifies that the 40-meter forest-area figure applies by classification, not as a uniform coastal no-build zone.

source_audit_support.source_locator: Article body lea-plan-003-06 normalized.md: 'PD 1067 states that banks of rivers and streams and shores of seas and lakes are subject to public-use easements: 3 m in urban areas, 20 m in agricultural areas, and 40 m in forest areas.' Common mistakes section warns against 'Using a 40 m water easement for every urban waterway.'

external_sources.citation: PD 1067 (Water Code of the Philippines), Article 51

proposed.text: According to PD 1067 (Water Code of the Philippines), Article 51, what public-use easement applies along the SHORES of the SEA in AGRICULTURAL areas?

rationale.a: Wrong. 3 meters is the PD 1067 Article 51 easement in URBAN areas, not agricultural.
rationale.b: Correct. PD 1067 Article 51 establishes a 20-meter public-use easement in AGRICULTURAL areas along banks of rivers/streams and shores of seas/lakes.
rationale.c: Wrong. 40 meters is the PD 1067 Article 51 easement in FOREST areas, not agricultural. The figure is set by land classification, not by a uniform no-build zone.
rationale.d: Wrong. 75 meters is not a PD 1067 easement figure.
rationale.correct: PD 1067 Article 51: easement of public use along banks of rivers/streams and shores of seas/lakes is 3 m (urban), 20 m (agricultural), or 40 m (forest). For agricultural shores the easement is 20 meters.
rationale.takeaway: PD 1067 easements are determined by LAND CLASSIFICATION (urban/agricultural/forest), not by water-body width or a uniform coastal no-build zone.

proposed.explanation: Article body: '3 m in urban areas, 20 m in agricultural areas, and 40 m in forest areas'. The post-Yolanda '40-meter no-build zone' was an administrative policy later revised; it is not the PD 1067 rule.
